data.name: Papu Papu
data.description:
Papu Papu is a recurring character in the Crash Bandicoot series, serving as the chief of the indigenous tribesmen residing in the Native Village on N. Sanity Island. He debuted as the first boss in Crash Bandicoot and has made subsequent appearances throughout the series.

== Appearance ==
Papu Papu is depicted as an obese, dark-skinned man and tribal chief. His attire varies slightly between games. In Crash Bandicoot, he wears a green skirt, red arm cuffs, a blue necklace, and a large totem mask that partially obscures his eyes. He also features red facial tattoos and prominent red lips. He typically carries a scepter topped with a skull and feathers.

== Personality ==
In the original Crash Bandicoot manual, Papu Papu is described as having a short temper. He is shown to be bilingual, speaking both English and his native language. His speech patterns differ across games: in Crash Team Racing, he uses third-person and omits pronouns, similar to Tiny Tiger; in Crash Twinsanity, he primarily speaks his native language. He is capable of racing and appears to possess some knowledge of magic.

Papu Papu's temperament is generally neutral, but he becomes aggressive when provoked. He is often found sleeping, and his confrontations with Crash usually stem from Crash's intrusion into his village, as seen in Crash Bandicoot and Crash Twinsanity. In Crash Bash, Uka Uka refers to him as an "old friend," and in Crash Team Racing, Uka Uka's invincibility mask takes the form of Papu Papu.

== Trivia ==
- Papu Papu's design and character are clearly inspired by stereotypical depictions of tribal chiefs.
- The differences in his speech between games add a layer of character evolution, even if unintentional.
- His role as the first boss in the original Crash Bandicoot makes him a memorable figure in the series' history.
- The fact that Uka Uka uses Papu Papu's image for his invincibility mask, shows that even evil powers find some use for the tribal leader.
